The fringes direction for all the oxides and crisscross fringes at the oxide matrix interface (Fig. 12 (d)) suggests that the oxides are incoherent with the matrix. Therefore dislocation bypasses to overcome the dispersed particles as observed from the inset image of Fig. 11(a).

mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning by Y2O3 dispersoids

evidence.quote: The dispersed Y2O3 particles at the interface strongly hinder the grain boundary migration and results in grain refinement.

The improved densification in high Y2O3 added sintered alloys is attributed to refined crystallite size, enhanced surface energy and grain boundary energy of W which facilitates faster diffusion (mass transfer along the neck region of W/solute atoms) and chemical activation for liquid phase sintering (MoNi, Ni3Ti phase formation) with respect to pore filling.
